vulnerabilities.title: INCOMPLETE_BLACKLIST_FILTER

root_cause.description: blacklist() is the sole security gate preventing execution of arbitrary attacker-controlled shellcode. It implements a blocklist (deny) approach that only rejects two specific byte values: 0x0f (first byte of 'syscall' instruction 0f 05) and 0xcd (opcode byte of 'int 0x80' instruction cd 80). A blocklist is inherently incomplete because it cannot anticipate all possible bypass techniques. The filter performs a static byte scan over the input buffer (indices 0-99) and does not prevent runtime construction of the blocked instruction encodings through arithmetic operations or other indirect means. Since the attacker fully controls the executed bytes (up to 99 bytes of shellcode), any bypass of this filter leads directly to arbitrary code execution. The filter blocks only the two standard Linux syscall instruction prefixes but does not constitute a comprehensive code-execution sandbox.

affected_objects: mmap'd shellcode buffer at 0x13370000 (100 bytes, R-X at execution time)

attack_surface.input: stdin shellcode (up to 99 bytes via read(0, buf, 0x63))
data_flow: stdin -> read(0, mmap_buf, 0x63) stores up to 99 bytes of attacker-controlled shellcode into mmap'd RWX region at 0x13370000
mmap_buf -> blacklist(mmap_buf) scans 100 bytes (indices 0-99), returns 1 if any byte == 0x0f or 0xcd, else returns 0
if blacklist returns 0 (pass) -> mprotect(mmap_buf, 0x64, R-X) makes region read-execute only
main zeroes all registers (rax-r15, rsp, rbp, xmm0-15), sets rdi=0x13370000, executes 'jmp rdi'
attacker-controlled bytes at 0x13370000 are executed as machine code with rdi=0x13370000 (known absolute address), rsp=0 (no stack), all other registers zeroed

security_check.expected: A comprehensive filter that prevents execution of any shellcode capable of invoking system calls or performing privileged operations, or alternatively an allowlist that only permits known-safe instruction sequences.
security_check.actual: A blocklist that rejects only two byte values (0x0f and 0xcd) out of 256 possible values. The filter checks each byte position independently without considering instruction semantics, runtime behavior, or alternative syscall mechanisms.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: The filter is a deny-list approach that blocks only the first bytes of 'syscall' (0x0f 0x05) and 'int 0x80' (0xcd 0x80). It does not account for: (1) runtime construction of blocked bytes via arithmetic in registers followed by writing to executable memory; (2) alternative x86-64 mechanisms for invoking system calls; (3) the fundamental weakness of blocklist-based filtering versus allowlist-based filtering. The filter is static (scans input bytes only) and does not prevent dynamic instruction generation at runtime.

vulnerable_operation.expression: jmp rdi (where rdi = [rbp-0x18] = 0x13370000, the mmap'd shellcode buffer containing attacker-controlled bytes that passed the incomplete blacklist filter)
vulnerable_operation.target: 0x13370000 (mmap'd shellcode execution region, R-X after mprotect)
vulnerable_operation.size: up to 99 bytes of attacker-controlled machine code

impact.reason: Attacker-controlled shellcode that passes the incomplete blacklist filter executes with full control of the instruction stream. The shellcode can perform arbitrary memory reads, writes, and computations within the constraints of the register state (rdi=0x13370000, rsp=0, all other GPRs=0). The incomplete filter allows shellcode that can bypass the 0x0f/0xcd byte restriction to execute arbitrary operations including memory corruption.

The shellcode runner design is intended to execute attacker-provided code. The blacklist filter is the only barrier. Since the filter is a blocklist that blocks only 2 of 256 byte values, it is bypassable by design (this is a CTF challenge). The exact bypass technique (how to invoke system calls without 0x0f or 0xcd bytes in the input, given the R-X memory protection) requires further analysis beyond static semantic review.

evidence.description: blacklist() scans 100 bytes (loop i=0 to i<=0x63 at 0x1335) checking each byte against 0x0f (cmp al,0xf at 0x1312) and 0xcd (cmp al,0xcd at 0x1326). Returns 1 if match found, 0 otherwise. This is the only input validation on shellcode content.

main calls blacklist(buf) at 0x1414, then checks 'test eax,eax; je 0x142c' at 0x1419-0x141b. If blacklist returns nonzero (reject), calls _abort('bye'). If zero (accept), proceeds to mprotect and execute. This confirms blacklist is the sole gate before code execution.

After mprotect and register zeroing, main executes 'jmp rdi' at 0x14ae where rdi=[rbp-0x18]=0x13370000 (loaded at 0x14a7). This transfers control to the attacker-controlled shellcode bytes that passed the incomplete filter.

The filter blocks only 0x0f and 0xcd (2 of 256 byte values). 0x0f is the prefix byte for all two-byte opcodes including syscall (0f 05) and sysenter (0f 34). 0xcd is the opcode for INT imm8 including int 0x80 (cd 80). However, the filter is a blocklist approach: it denies specific bytes rather than allowing only safe ones. Blocklist filters are inherently incomplete because they cannot anticipate all bypass vectors. The filter does not prevent runtime construction of blocked bytes through register arithmetic.

After blacklist passes, mprotect(buf,0x64,4) at 0x143d changes region to R-X (not writable). All registers zeroed (0x1442-0x14a3) except rdi=0x13370000. rsp=0 means no stack. The shellcode executes with these constraints. The R-X protection prevents direct self-modifying code, but the filter's incompleteness means bypass techniques exist that work within these constraints.

Verify whether the mmap hint 0x13370000 is reliably honored at runtime (affects whether shellcode base address is predictable)
Determine if seccomp or other external sandbox is active at runtime (would affect impact severity)
Verify whether adjacent pages to the mmap region are writable (could enable self-modifying code bypass)

vulnerabilities.title: READ_RETURN_VALUE_CHECK_INCOMPLETE

root_cause.description: main() checks read()'s return value only against zero (EOF/empty input) using 'cmp DWORD PTR [rbp-0x1c], 0x0; jne'. A negative return value (indicating an error such as EINTR) is nonzero and passes the check, causing execution to continue. When read() returns -1 (error), no bytes are written to the buffer, but the buffer was previously memset to 0, so the shellcode region contains 100 zero bytes. The program then proceeds to blacklist (which passes, since 0x00 is not 0x0f or 0xcd), mprotect, and execute the all-zero buffer as code.

root_cause.description: main() uses two different sources for the shellcode buffer address. All data operations (mmap return stored at [rbp-0x10], memset, read, blacklist, mprotect) use the mmap() return value stored at [rbp-0x10]. However, the final 'jmp rdi' instruction loads rdi from [rbp-0x18], which is a compile-time constant 0x13370000 set at 0x1364 ('mov QWORD PTR [rbp-0x18], 0x13370000'). If mmap() returns an address different from the hint 0x13370000 (because MAP_FIXED is not used, only a hint), the shellcode is read into and filtered at the actual mmap address, but execution jumps to the constant 0x13370000 which may be unmapped or contain different data.

attack_surface.input: N/A (internal address handling, not directly attacker-controlled)
data_flow: 0x1396: call mmap@plt with hint=0x13370000, flags=0x22 (no MAP_FIXED)
0x139b: mov QWORD PTR [rbp-0x10], rax (mmap return stored separately)
0x14a7: mov rdi, QWORD PTR [rbp-0x18] (loads CONSTANT, not mmap return)
0x14ae: jmp rdi (jumps to 0x13370000, not necessarily the mmap'd address)

security_check.expected: The jmp target should use the same address as the mmap return value ([rbp-0x10]) that was used for all other operations, or MAP_FIXED should be used to guarantee the hint address is granted.
security_check.actual: The jmp target uses [rbp-0x18] (compile-time constant 0x13370000) while all other operations use [rbp-0x10] (mmap return value). These may differ if the kernel does not honor the mmap hint.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing consistency between the mmap return value used for data operations and the jump target address. No verification that mmap returned the requested hint address.

vulnerable_operation.expression: mov rdi, QWORD PTR [rbp-0x18] (0x13370000 constant); jmp rdi — uses constant instead of [rbp-0x10] (mmap return)
vulnerable_operation.target: 0x13370000 (compile-time constant, may differ from actual mmap'd address)

impact.reason: If mmap() returns an address different from 0x13370000 (hint not honored by kernel), the jmp rdi at 0x14ae jumps to 0x13370000 which may be unmapped memory. This causes a SIGSEGV. The shellcode was correctly read into and filtered at the actual mmap address, but execution goes to the wrong address. In practice, the kernel usually honors low hint addresses, so this crash path is unlikely but possible.

evidence.description: At 0x1364: 'mov QWORD PTR [rbp-0x18], 0x13370000' stores the compile-time constant address. This is separate from the mmap return value.

At 0x139b: 'mov QWORD PTR [rbp-0x10], rax' stores the mmap() return value at [rbp-0x10]. All subsequent data operations (memset at 0x13b5, read at 0x13df, blacklist at 0x140d, mprotect at 0x142c) use [rbp-0x10].

At 0x14a7: 'mov rdi, QWORD PTR [rbp-0x18]' loads the compile-time constant 0x13370000 (NOT [rbp-0x10] which holds the mmap return). Then 0x14ae: 'jmp rdi' jumps to this constant. If mmap returned a different address, the jump target is inconsistent with where the shellcode was actually stored.

mmap is called with flags 0x22 (MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS) without MAP_FIXED (0x10). Without MAP_FIXED, the address parameter is only a hint; the kernel may return a different address. This makes the inconsistency between [rbp-0x18] (constant) and [rbp-0x10] (mmap return) a potential runtime issue.

verification_required: Confirm at runtime whether mmap(0x13370000, ...) actually returns 0x13370000 or a different address
If mmap returns a different address, confirm that jmp to 0x13370000 causes SIGSEGV (unmapped) or executes stale/wrong data

non_vulnerabilities.description: init() calls setvbuf(stdin/stdout/stderr, 0, _IONBF, 0) and alarm(60). These are standard I/O setup and timeout configuration.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: No security-relevant input handling or memory operations. setvbuf parameters are hardcoded constants. alarm(60) sets a process timeout but does not create a vulnerability. All parameters are compile-time constants with no attacker control.

non_vulnerabilities.description: _abort(msg) calls printf('%s', msg) then exit(1). Used for fatal error paths (mmap failed, read failed, blacklist violation).
non_vulnerabilities.reason: printf uses '%s' format specifier with a string argument (not a format string vulnerability — the format string is hardcoded at 0x2008 as '%s'). The msg parameter is always a hardcoded string literal from .rodata, not attacker-controlled. exit(1) terminates the process cleanly.

non_vulnerabilities.description: main checks mmap() return value against MAP_FAILED (-1) at 0x139f: 'cmp QWORD PTR [rbp-0x10], 0xffffffffffffffff; jne 0x13b5'. If mmap fails, calls _abort('mmap failed!').
non_vulnerabilities.reason: This is a correct check. mmap() returns MAP_FAILED (-1) on failure, and the code correctly compares against this value and aborts. No vulnerability here.

non_vulnerabilities.description: main installs a stack canary at 0x134e (mov rax, fs:0x28 -> [rbp-0x8]) and checks it at 0x14b5-0x14c4 before returning.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: Stack canary is correctly installed and verified. However, note that the canary check at 0x14b5 is on the 'normal return' path which is unreachable in practice — the function never returns normally because it ends with 'jmp rdi' (0x14ae) which transfers control to shellcode. The code after jmp rdi (0x14b0-0x14ca) is dead code unless the shellcode somehow returns to 0x14b0. The canary provides no protection against the shellcode execution path.

non_vulnerabilities.description: The binary has only one NEEDED library (libc.so.6) with no RPATH/RUNPATH. LD_LIBRARY_PATH would take precedence over the system path.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: While LD_LIBRARY_PATH precedence is a theoretical environment-level concern, in the challenge context there is no evidence of malicious library substitution. The binary runs in a controlled environment with the system libc. This is not a binary-level vulnerability but an environment configuration consideration. Standard library resolution from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6.

unresolved.description: Exact bypass technique for the blacklist filter (BUG-001) is not determined by static analysis alone.
unresolved.reason: The blacklist blocks 0x0f and 0xcd bytes. After mprotect, the region is R-X (not writable), preventing direct self-modifying code. rsp=0 means no stack. The exact method to invoke a system call without 0x0f/0xcd bytes in the input, within these constraints, requires dynamic analysis or creative shellcode engineering beyond static semantic review.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3/S4 should perform dynamic analysis to determine the specific bypass technique: (1) test whether adjacent pages to the mmap region are writable; (2) test whether the mmap hint is reliably honored; (3) explore x86-64 instruction encoding alternatives; (4) test self-modifying code feasibility if any writable+executable memory is found.

unresolved.description: Whether seccomp or other external sandbox is active at runtime.
unresolved.reason: No seccomp/prctl symbols found in the binary, but an external sandbox could be applied by the challenge infrastructure. If seccomp is active, the impact of shellcode execution may be limited (e.g., no execve, no open/read/write).
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 should check for seccomp at runtime (e.g., via /proc/self/status Seccomp field or seccomp-tools).

unresolved.description: Whether the mmap hint 0x13370000 is reliably granted by the kernel at runtime.
unresolved.reason: mmap uses a hint without MAP_FIXED. The kernel usually honors low hints, but under ASLR or memory pressure, it may return a different address. This affects BUG-004 (jmp target inconsistency) and the predictability of the shellcode base address for the attacker.
unresolved.required_next_step: S3 should run the binary multiple times and check whether mmap consistently returns 0x13370000.
